conviction_note: The print is about solvency, not the quarter. The quarter was pre-guided on 10 Sep, and the Q4 fuel hit is visible in every peer, so it is largely in a stock that is down 45% in 20 days. Sourced liquidity arithmetic (about $2.2B cash plus $0.8B undrawn lines at Q2, against a $750M covenant) and 27-30% of float short lean slightly up. A creditor co-op with bonds at 42-45 cents and +9.6 vol points of put skew lean down. p_up 52 on an abs move of 20, so the scaled number is +0.8 against an impact_sum of +1.7. They agree in sign. The sum is larger because the positioning finding carries squeeze mechanics that p_up deliberately holds near 50.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after JetBlue's 10 Sep update beat their own revenue guides. Southwest's Q3 RASM was +21.6% against a 17.5-19.5% guide (8-K 21 Oct). American's revenue was +19.3%, 'above the high end' of its guide. Their fuel prices landed where JetBlue guided: LUV $3.92/gal, ALK $3.94, against JBLU's $3.96 guide. That points to JetBlue's RASM at or above the top of its +17-20% range, against a consensus of $2.82B that sits near the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: a narrow beat (-$0.66 against -$0.70, RASM +10.9%) bought +10.5%. Oct 2025 -11.9% and Jan 2026 -6.9% were driven by the outlook. The quarter line on its own has bought a modest positive here.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $2.82B equals the midpoint of the 10 Sep guide, which has not been re-marked for peers' upside. If it had, revenue estimates would sit at about $2.85-2.87B, the top of the guide. This is a peer proxy and the quarter is mostly inside the guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: American's Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006201/000000620126000064/a8kerexhibit991q3-26.htm): revenue +19.3%, above the high end of its guide. Alaska's unit revenue was +12% (https://finsee.ai/earnings/alk/2026/q3/en/). These are separate documents from the LUV 8-K.

findings.finding: The FY 2026 adjusted operating margin guide of (2)% to (5)% assumed $3.49/gal fuel and was not updated on 10 Sep. Peers' Q4 fuel guides now sit at $4.55-4.85/gal: AAL about $4.70 on the 19 Oct curve, ALK $4.65-4.85, LUV $4.55. JetBlue does not hedge, so the release almost certainly cuts the FY guide and gives a Q4 with a deep loss. At about 210M Q4 gallons, fuel alone adds roughly $250M+ over a $3.49 basis. Every peer offset part of this with Q4 revenue of about +20% (AAL +19.5% to 22.5%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook-driven prints: Oct 2025 -11.86% and Jan 2026 -6.89%. Jan 2025 -25.7% came on a capacity and cost guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The peers' cuts (Delta 9 Oct, ALK 20 Oct, LUV 21 Oct, AAL 22 Oct, United) are public, and the stock fell 45% over the same weeks. What is not yet visible is JetBlue's own number and whether its RASM offset matches peers. Kept negative but small because the short is crowded.
findings.independence: Alaska guided Q4 to a loss of $2.00-2.50 at $4.65-4.85 fuel (https://finsee.ai/earnings/alk/2026/q3/en/). findings.finding: Per the Q2 10-Q, the company-level liquidity is far above the covenant the distress narrative turns on. Total liquidity was $2.2B in cash and investments, plus an undrawn $600M Citibank revolver (maturing 2029), an undrawn Morgan Stanley line of about $200M, and a $250M incremental option on the April aircraft facility. On top of that come up to $105M of IAE credits. The TrueBlue minimum-liquidity covenant is $750M at quarter end. UBS (19 Oct, upgraded to Neutral) estimates about $660M of H2 burn and about $1.6B of year-end liquidity. Scheduled principal is only $236M for the rest of 2026 and $478M in 2027. The 10-Q carries no going-concern language. The release and 10-Q will give the 30 Sep figure, the first company number since the creditor co-op was reported on 23 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior JetBlue print with a liquidity scare of this size. Jan 2025 (-25.7%) and Oct 2025 (-11.9%) fell on the outlook, not on liquidity.
findings.why_not_priced: Equity at about $850M market cap, the record low, and loyalty-secured bonds at 42-45c price meaningful odds of a restructuring soon. If the market were pricing the documented $2.2B plus $0.8B undrawn against a $750M floor and 2026-27 maturities under $0.75B, the 2031 bonds would not have lost 35 points in three weeks with no new company number. The two-sided range reflects that management may confirm an exchange or liability-management plan instead.
findings.independence: UBS note via MarketScreener, 2026-10-19 (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/jetblue-airways-has-sufficient-near-term-liquidity-despite-higher-jet-fuel-prices-ubs-says-ce785cdbdd8ff623). S&P (June, CCC+) also says liquidity and borrowing capacity are sufficient (https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/jetblue-lenders-organize-stock-debt-231841700.html). The maturity schedule is from https://viewfromthewing.com/jetblue-creditors-hire-bankruptcy-advisers-as-2-billion-in-frequent-flyer-debt-hits-42-cents-on-the-dollar/. The numbers come from one 10-Q; the conclusion that liquidity is sufficient comes from separate sources.

findings.finding: Crowded short into a binary print. 26.6% of float was short at 30 Sep (98.0M shares, up 2%), with reports of 30%+ by mid-October. The stock is -45% over 20 days and -21% over 5 days, at a record low. Any reassuring liquidity or financing statement on a 10:00 ET call meets about 3.4 days of short cover. The last bmo print with an in-line or better quarter (Jul 2026) bought +10.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: +10.5% on a modest beat after a weak run-in. Up on 4 of 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+9.6) and put/call OI of 2.61 show the options market positioned for further downside, not for a squeeze. If a squeeze were priced, call skew would be bid and the stock would not be closing at its lows into the event.

findings.finding: Creditors holding the $2B 9.875% 2031 TrueBlue-secured notes and the $742M first-lien loan have organized with PJT Partners and Akin Gump (WSJ/Bloomberg, 23 Oct). The bonds and loan are at about 42-45c, from about 80c in early October. Co-ops form in anticipation of a liability-management exercise. If management says on the call that it has engaged its own advisers or is pursuing an exchange, the equity faces dilution risk. JetBlue has said only that it is 'confident in its strategy'.

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Monday's -16% was this news. What is not priced is the company's answer, which the call will force. Sized small because the short is crowded and the headline is already in the tape.

findings.why_not_priced: Almost fully priced: public for two months and the stock has halved since. It is filed because it removes a holder who might backstop an equitization.

findings.finding: In October the FAA gave final approval for JetBlue's $58.5M purchase of 22 former Spirit LaGuardia slots, with minimum-use requirements waived through April 2027. The 10-Q conditions had a deadline of 31 Oct 2026. The approval adds New York capacity in a market Spirit has exited, at a small cash cost.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and public. Management may frame it on the call as a 2027 revenue lever. It is cash out ($58.5M) at a moment the market cares about cash.

outside_window.finding: The large debt maturities come later: 2029 principal is $1.835B, and CreditSights warned of a potential liquidity crunch by late 2027. The solvency question extends well past this print.

baseline_tension: The net sign (+) runs against the +9.6 put skew and a P/C OI of 2.61. The explicit reason is that the stock is down 45% into the print with 27-30% of float short, so a liquidity number at or above the documented Q2 cushion meets a crowded short. That caveat holds p_up at 52, not higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 7, crowded short (26.6-30% of float): the guidance negative shrank from -2.0 to -1.5 and the creditor negative from -1.5 to -1.0. The positive sign against the +9.6 skew stays only with the explicit squeeze reason in baseline_tension.
Rules 5 and 'What has worked' (covenant arithmetic is inference, not a document number): the liquidity finding shrank from +2.0 to +1.5. It rests on 10-Q numbers, but its conclusion is arithmetic.
Rule 6 (the finding lands inside the 10 Sep guide): the peer read-through on the quarter shrank from +1.0 to +0.7.

Rule 3 (read the set): the liquidity-sufficient and creditor-co-op findings can both be true (near-term liquidity against medium-term restructuring), so both are kept with offsetting signs. p_up and abs_move were unchanged.
